entities.name: Around the World in Eighty Days
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Around the World in Eighty Days is a seminal novel by Jules Verne that chronicles the journey of Phileas Fogg as he attempts to circumnavigate the globe in record time. Published in 1872, this groundbreaking work of science fiction not only captivated readers with its vivid descriptions of exotic locales and technological innovations but also reflected the anxieties and aspirations of the Victorian era.

The novel's central premise – a gentleman's wager that he can traverse the globe in just eighty days – serves as a microcosm for the era's obsession with speed, progress, and global connectivity. Through Fogg's perilous journey, Verne explores themes of class, identity, and the human condition, ultimately positing that despite our differences, we are all connected across borders and cultures.

The novel's impact extends far beyond its initial publication, influencing generations of writers, scientists, and thinkers. Its influence can be seen in films like 'Around the World in 80 Days' (2004) starring Steve Coogan, as well as in contemporary works such as Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by Douglas Adams.

The legacy of Around the World in Eighty Days continues to resonate with readers today, offering a timeless blend of adventure, intellectual curiosity, and emotional resonance. As we navigate an increasingly interconnected world, Verne's vision of global citizenship and the power of human ingenuity remains as relevant as ever.

"The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page," Verne wrote in his novel. This quote encapsulates the essence of Around the World in Eighty Days – a testament to the transformative power of exploration, discovery, and the boundless potential that lies within us all.

For scholars and readers alike, Around the World in Eighty Days remains an essential work of historical literature, a window into the minds and values of the Victorian era, and a powerful reminder of our shared human experiences across cultures and time.
